newsitem.title: CANADA: Bell Canada applies to hike rural rates.
newsitem.headline: Bell Canada applies to hike rural rates.

text.p: BCE Inc's telephone unit, Bell Canada, said on Friday it applied to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission to increase the local phone rates of about three million customers in rural to medium-sized communities by C$0.45 to C$4.

The telephone giant, which serves Ontario and Quebec, applied to increase charges so it can upgrade the switching technology serving of about 490,000 of its non-urban customers. If approved, the increases would add an average C$1.11 a month to local phone bills on December 1 for about 40 percent of Bell's seven million residential clients.
Larger communities would generally face smaller hikes, while customers in Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa and Quebec City would not see any increase, Bell said.
It said local service prices for business customers would not change under the plan, but were being addressed under a separate proposal that Bell announced in December 1995.

Bell said the extra money would be used to invest C$180 million in new equipment that would allow people living in rural areas, small towns and medium-sized cities to have services equivalent to those in large cities, including better connection to data services and the Internet.
The company wants to complete the upgrading of equipment by December 1997.
Residential customers across Canada also face a C$2-a-month rate increase for local service on January 1, which was approved by the federal regulator last year.
